# BrewMenu

> BrewMenu is a free, open-source native macOS menu bar app for Homebrew. It keeps an eye on Homebrew for you — outdated packages, `brew doctor` warnings, cleanups and services — and upgrades everything in one click, by running the real `brew` you already have.

BrewMenu is made by Nicolás Jiménez, who goes by dotfn: a software developer from Argentina (https://dotfn.dev). It is not affiliated with the Homebrew project.

## Key facts

- Price: free. No account, no sign-up.
- License: GNU AGPL-3.0 (open source).
- Requires: macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later, and Homebrew at /opt/homebrew (Apple silicon), /usr/local (Intel), or a custom path set in Settings.
- Install with Homebrew (recommended; it keeps the app updated): `brew install --cask dotfn/tap/brewmenu`
- Or download the signed .zip from GitHub Releases: https://github.com/dotfn/brewmenu/releases/latest (signed but not notarized yet: on first open, macOS may ask you to allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway; installing with Homebrew avoids this).
- Update: `brew upgrade --cask brewmenu`, or from BrewMenu itself, which offers a restart after upgrading itself.
- Uninstall: `brew uninstall --cask brewmenu` (add `--zap` to also delete its settings and history).
- Privacy: no telemetry. Its only network requests go to formulae.brew.sh, for package descriptions, trending packages and install counts.
- Languages: English and Spanish, following the system language.

## What it does

- Updates, counted: the menu bar icon shows how many upgrades are waiting; each package shows the installed version and the next one.
- Upgrades you can watch: `brew upgrade` output streams line by line, for one package or all of them; Cancel stops it mid-run. If one package fails in an Upgrade All, it says which and retries just that one.
- `brew doctor`, read for you: checked once a day; each warning is shown with how to fix it.
- Services: see which `brew services` are running and start or stop them without a terminal.
- Cleanup, sized first: a dry run measures what `brew cleanup` and `brew autoremove` would free before you confirm.
- Insights from 30 days of history: stale upgrades, a doctor check that hasn't run, a service that went down.
- Dashboard: one window for everything installed — apps and command-line tools, every tap with its packages, and what each one takes on disk; search and add a formula, cask or tap.
- Your schedule: checks every hour by default, or every 6 hours, daily, or only when you ask.
- Quiet notifications for new updates, doctor warnings and finished upgrades, throttled so they don't pile up. The menu bar icon can hide itself when nothing needs attention.

## How it works

BrewMenu does not replace or reimplement Homebrew. Every action runs the actual `brew` command and shows its output as it arrives, and it reads your existing Cellar. The command line keeps working exactly as before, and nothing BrewMenu does is hidden from it.
